_comment: `b.js` imports `x.js`, then the lazy host `a.js`, then `y.js`. Native ESM runs `x`, `a`, `y`, `b`. Without `preserveModules`, `x.js` is in the chunk of `b.js` and runs in its body. An init at the import of the host would run `a` before `x`, so `x.js` moves to a new common chunk before the import of the host. The chunk of `b.js` then initializes `a.js` right after that import. With `preserveModules`, the file of `x.js` runs `x` at load, before the import of the host.
